increment_paragraph: **CMT-GETTER-OWNERSHIP-CLOSURE (2026-10-26).** The [card](../../reports/cmt-getter-ownership-closure/README.md) validates a reachable resource-custody violation in the pinned CMetrics labeled getter path. The NUL-free metric name `42 d5 68 e1 38 d7 27 ff` has XXH3 digest zero; one empty label preserves the stream, selects the embedded metric, allocates histogram storage without setting `metric_static_set`, and reaches map destruction without freeing that storage. Fresh BASE/planner preceded prediction and implementation. The first TIP attempt was unchanged because the source adapter refused Clang's canonical `((void*)0)` expansion; the corrected, fail-closed adapter accepts only literal `NULL` or that exact zero spelling and rejects a nonzero control. Final paired corpus changes exactly `cmt_map_metric_get` Unknown to provisional Unsafe: 1,013 Safe / 3,812 Unknown / 9 provisional Unsafe becomes 1,013 / 3,811 / 10. System remains 101 / 343 / 4 and slice remains 57 Safe / 4 Pending / 342 Unknown / 1 provisional Unsafe because neither configured selection contains the getter row, so the prediction for those routes misses. All NULL projections and all other semantic rows are unchanged after exact evidence-version and observation-only reading attribution. Matching generic Rust ownership state, placeholder-free Lean proofs and canonical CFL/CMetrics `.qv` models preserve fail-closed executable adoption; parsing a model grants no call permission.

ledger.text: CMT-GETTER-OWNERSHIP-CLOSURE adds a source-bound analyzer adapter for one complete pinned getter counterexample and changes that row to provisional Unsafe. It does not turn cmetrics/map_lifetime.qv, opts_lifetime.qv or setter declarations into executable summaries, and it supplies no generic checked consumer for copied/retained inputs, nested ownership, index/cache aliases, expiration or partial cleanup. Those adoption obligations remain Open.

ledger.title: Add pinned shorthand bundles for repeated provider contract requirements
ledger.text: CMetrics and CFL contracts repeat long require lists. Add explicitly declared, provider-owned requirement bundles such as `contract_cmetrics_resource_v1` and `contract_cfl_resource_v1` whose expansion is pinned by exact clause identity, order and provenance. Missing, unknown, cyclic, duplicate or signature-mismatched bundles must refuse. A bundle is syntax-level requirement expansion only: it is not an alias for executable `resource_contract_v1`, supplies no call permission and cannot weaken Unknown. DISCHARGE: matching parser/formatter and Rust semantic support, placeholder-free Lean definitions/theorems, canonical `.qv` declarations, provider inventory/count/load-path pins, mutation controls for every refusal and fresh native attribution if any verdict-bearing semantics move.
